A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIG method and selective-training study. All 20 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, VIG analyses, attention and textual-corruption evaluations, qualitative examples, and selection ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds another model and training dataset, additional benchmarks, and new diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: The blurred-image VIG calculation, top-p% sample selection, shared sample/token threshold, and loss masking with full answer context remain unchanged. Applying this procedure to Open-Qwen2VL adds an experimental configuration, not a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds MAmmoTH-VL instruction-training data and CV-Bench evaluation covering foundational 2D and 3D visual reasoning. It also introduces text-only evaluation on GSM8K, MMLU, HellaSwag, and TruthfulQA, substantially expanding the evaluated task requirements. Existing benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: VCD is newly included in the VQAv2 textual-corruption comparison in Table E.1, although it already appeared in the general benchmark comparison. Table 3 also adds a vanilla Open-Qwen2VL 2B counterpart. The original VCD, PAI, VAR, and LACING comparisons in Table 4 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a distinct Open-Qwen2VL 2B training configuration using a random 1M MAmmoTH-VL subset, with 701K samples retained. New evaluation procedures include combined accuracy across CV-Bench tasks, corpus-level POS aggregation, and category-retention analysis using 20%/60%/20% frequency tiers. These extend the experimental design; settings for retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine VIG by POS category, preservation of text-only capabilities, retention of rare concepts and different training-task categories, and robustness relative to VCD under textual corruption. Appendix A adds five matched/partially matched/conflicting-image examples. The original selection-level and selection-ratio ablations are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run or seed counts, significance tests, or defined confidence intervals. Existing distribution plots and attention bands retain their reporting practices; the added experiments do not introduce new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results while preserving shared Table 3 values and all Table 4 scores. Newly reported Open-Qwen2VL results show 4.10B versus 2.42B active tokens and CV-Bench accuracy of 68.99 versus 70.01 for vanilla versus VIG training. Added results include text-only scores, POS and retention findings, qualitative VIG scores, and VCD's corruption-normalized score of 42.9 versus VIG's 54.1.

T1.justification: The VIG definition, cross-entropy/KL derivation, deterministic-supervision assumption, token decomposition, selection-set definitions, and CHAIR formulas remain mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: VIG measures visual dependence, identifies grounded tokens, and enables efficient selective training with improved grounding. The added experiments support these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning preserved linguistic competence and long-tail coverage, explaining these through unchanged text-only supervision, full input context, and selection by visual necessity. It also interprets the Qwen and VCD results as evidence of architectural generality and representation-level debiasing. The original computational-overhead limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds the Open-Qwen2VL checkpoint reference, its selection threshold of 0.012, and training details including one epoch, batch size 128, learning rate 2e-5, AdamW, and ten-hour training time. Existing implementation disclosures are retained. Detailed text-only evaluation and POS-tagging instructions remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Open-Qwen2VL, MAmmoTH-VL, Cambrian-1/CV-Bench, and the four text-only benchmarks. It extends the empirical positioning against VCD under textual corruption. The related-work narrative and principal novelty positioning otherwise remain stable; citation-style and bibliographic corrections are presentation changes.

P1.justification: The title gains 'Focusing Where Vision Matters,' author and publication information changes, and new analysis paragraphs, an initial qualitative appendix, and an Impact Statement are added. Most existing prose, contribution statements, and section ordering remain intact rather than undergoing extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, relocating and resizing figures and tables throughout. Table 3 gains model rows and a CV-Bench column; Figure 2 gains CV-Bench. New displays include the POS plot, text-only and VCD tables, qualitative image grid, and two-panel retention figure.

improvement.justification: The Open-Qwen2VL/MAmmoTH-VL experiment substantially strengthens generalization evidence beyond v1's closely related LLaVA/ShareGPT4V models. Corpus-level token and retention analyses, plus the VCD corruption comparison, address important questions about selection behavior and robustness. These gains strengthen the empirical case, although unexplained identical 7B/13B text-only rows in Tables 5 and E.2 weaken that evidence, and the earlier main/appendix ablation discrepancies persist in Tables 6 and F.1.
